column1: # Spike S2.7's disclosed list (docs/adr/0003-webview-network.md): traffic the
# app sets off that nothing it controls can stop. The check reports what an
# entry covers as "disclosed", in a summary row of its own, instead of
# failing on it; docs/privacy.md must disclose each entry verbatim (roadmap
# M6, item 6). Anything an entry does not cover still fails, and so does an
# entry's traffic in an OS or phase it does not name. An entry names only
# the phases its traffic was seen in. No entry may cover the app's own
# process tree (navaja, WebKit's processes, msedgewebview2.exe).
# One entry a line, five tab-separated fields:
#   os       macos or windows
#   phases   idle, in-use, or both, separated by a space
#   service  the system service that sent it. macOS: the process the packet
#            was for, as pktap names it (its eproc, else its proc).
#            Windows: the service's identity, as the review list names it
#            ("svchost.exe [wlidsvc]").
#   hosts    the DNS names its lookups asked for, comma-separated. Every name
#            a packet is tied to must be one of them:
#            - macOS: a DNS packet, the name it asks for; any other packet,
#              the names that mDNSResponder looked up for the same process
#              (name and PID), in the phase, before the connection began,
#              and that gave its remote address. A name stands for the
#              names whose CNAMEs lead to it, as far as the job's captures
#              show, so an entry may list a CNAME's target too.
#            - Windows: the names its process asked the DNS client for (its
#              log's event 3008), in the phase, before the connection, in
#              lookups that gave its remote address.
#   purpose  what it is for, as privacy.md says it
macos
column5: the data that macOS's webprivacyd service fetches from Apple when WebKit asks it for its storage-access quirk lists (fixes for particular websites, for how they reach their cookies across sites)

column1: macos
column5: the certificate check (OCSP) that macOS's trustd makes for webprivacyd's connection to wps.apple.com

column1: windows
column5: Windows' Microsoft-account sign-in service, which contacts Microsoft's sign-in server within seconds of the app's start, though no log names the app or WebView2 as asking for it
